Once again my dog Albert had great treatment from Medivet in Acton. He goes regularly for his arthritis injection and loves going.  He always receives a lot of attention and kindness from everyone.

We had the worst experience at this clinic and would not recommend it to anyone.

Firstly, there appears to be very poor communication between the vets. We visited several times within a short period and saw a different vet on each occasion. Every time, we were asked the same questions and often given conflicting information compared with the previous consultation. It felt completely disorganised and lacking in continuity of care.

We then had a terrible experience with one of the receptionists, who was extremely rude when we requested to see a different vet. At one point, she told us: “If you want to see another vet, then go somewhere else.”

We are also paying for the Medivet+ plan, which turned out to be a complete waste of money. When we said we would follow her suggestion and move to another clinic, therefore cancelling the plan, the first thing she said was: “I’m going to charge the remaining balance of the plan anyway.” Rather than trying to de-escalate the situation or help resolve our concerns, her focus seemed entirely on money.

She also repeatedly threatened us by saying: “I will sack you, I will sack you”, which we understood to mean removing our pet from the system. To make matters worse, she refused to give us her name.

We submitted an official complaint through their own process, but it appears they do not know how to handle complaints properly.

Overall, this has been an incredibly stressful and upsetting experience, especially when trying to care for a pet that requires medical attention.
I really like Acton Lane Vets. The look after my cats so well.
Friendly, professional, welcoming  and appointment on time. A great combination.
Friendly vet practice & staff are nice too.

My cat Picchu was recently lethargic and off his food and I got an appointment the day I called. Valentina soon found a lump in his abdomen and was able to do an ultrasound there and then and confirmed that he has a lymphoma. Obviously this is a shock as he is only 10, but it was so helpful to know the facts so quickly so that we could decide how to go forward. Valentina and Vesi couldn’t have been more helpful, informative and sympathetic, which makes this sad experience much more bearable.

This clinic needs to be reported to the competent authorities for overcharging clients.

I want to share my experience with Medivet Acton. My dog was diagnosed with a heart murmur and will need to take three medications for the rest of his life. In the first month, I bought the medicines from them and paid £202 for just 30 days, while these three medications, the exact quantity on the petdrugsonline website, cost £54. I was shocked by the percentage of profit they make on this. I contacted them the following month and requested the prescription, which cost £53 for only three months. They refused to prescribe the medications for six months, considering my dog will need to take them for the rest of his life. They only want to profit and don't care about your dog's health. I requested a refund for the prescription and will try my luck with another vet.

We now do monthly injections to ease any pain he may have. The team at Acton Lane Veterinary Surgery are absolutely amazing and incredibly kind  - the vet is so gorgeous with my cat - she strokes him and talks to him like he is her cat while giving him his medication, which i love!
it wasn't a problem to book a visit and my dog received very good professional help, thank you

Deeply Frustrated and Upset with My Experience at this clinic

I want to share my recent experience because I left this clinic feeling extremely disrespected, anxious, and angry.

I went there to microchip my cat. It’s the closest vet to my home, and I had my 7-month-old baby with me — so just getting there was already a challenge.

When I arrived, the front door was locked, and I could clearly see the receptionist (a man) talking to a customer inside. I rang the bell and waited outside for over 5 minutes in full view of the staff. Still, no one came to open the door. Eventually, the customer (not a staff member) came and kindly opened the door for me.

I sat down and waited quietly, holding my baby and keeping my cat calm. I waited there for 40 minutes, and during that entire time, the receptionist was still speaking to the same customer — even continuing the conversation after it made the customer cry. I overheard the receptionist ask if she wanted a hug, which she declined. It was clear this wasn’t a quick conversation — but at no point did the receptionist acknowledge me, say hello, or even offer a moment of courtesy to someone visibly waiting with a baby and a pet.

Eventually, another staff member came out and asked how she could help. I explained I was there to get my cat microchipped and asked if that was possible today. She said, “Yes, if it’s just a microchip,” and asked me to sit and wait again — which I did, for another 10 minutes.

Finally, I approached the receptionist myself, only to be told I had to fill out an online form and that there were no appointments available until the 23rd of June— about 14 days from the day I walked in.

I was shocked. Why was none of this communicated when I first walked in? I had been sitting there for over an hour, and the receptionist didn’t even acknowledge me or inform me there was no availability. This whole situation could have been avoided with the smallest amount of courtesy and communication.

I left feeling totally dismissed and angry. It’s hard enough being a parent and pet owner — I expected a vet clinic to be more empathetic and professional, especially when I made the effort to come in person.

I wanted to share my disappointing experience with MediVet in Acton. We were excited to register at this vet as it is close to our house.

I had registered my puppy a few weeks ago in anticipation of booking his his first appt and second vaccinations. I went in person and the receptionist had asked for dates he had his first vaccinations and we landed on the 10th Apr being the date he needed his second jabs.

I called the day prior (9th) to confirm the appt as I had not heard anything. I was then told that the appt was not actually on the 10th, it was scheduled for the 16th, which was news to me and that there was no room to fit us in for the remainder of the week. I then found out that he HAD to get his jabs on the 10th as we would have had to start the process all over again!

I scrambled around to register at another vet to get an appt in, which luckily another local vet was able to fit us in on the 10th.

The receptionist at MediVet then called me and said that she "just wanted the week to end" when I had asked her how she was. She said that they would be able to fit us in, but only at 5pm on the 10th.

I then stated that I was pretty disappointed with the situation and we could have had a puppy stuck inside for another 8 weeks because of this scheduling mistake. I said we were going to another vet and she said that "it is good we're going to another vet as they already have enough clients."

This comment was extremely rude and unprofessional.

I would avoid this practice.
